notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on PRB_010 (root cause in fix_notes or worknotes; status fix_in_progress), the change CHG_026 (MDM text, new, SVC_001, CI_084, GROUP_008, priority and implementation_plan not null) and the three notifications on INC_073 (Joanne Simpson, Brandon Davis, Carl Brown; type update, status sent, message not null), with six of the seven benchmark checks kept by both.
disagreement: disposition of verify_change_linked: A kept, carried by one requirement selecting a mapping row with change_id, incident_id and problem_id together; B repaired, carried by two requirements (change to problem, change to incident) selected by natural key so that one row or two would pass; chose A's kept form because the benchmark's check is the prior, the schema's ck_crm_incident_or_problem is an OR (one row may hold both links), and the seed's one-link-per-row mappings are precedent rather than contradiction; B's form would also pass a two-row state the benchmark fails (logged on the requirement).
disagreement: cell format: B wrote the two-phrase cells (fix_notes, worknotes, short_description, description) as one compound string each ('LIKE ... OR LIKE ...'); rewritten as lists of predicates, as A has them; the sql, identical in both passes, carries the OR and is authoritative. B also left the selector columns (incident_id, email) out of the notification cells where A repeats them; A's form kept, same tested content.
The change table has no type column, so policy 4.2's standard/normal/emergency type is untestable. INC_073.problem is null on the seed although PRB_010.original_task = INC_073; the policy's incident_to_problem linking rule is not written as a requirement because the request does not ask for it and no listed tool updates incidents. The 'appropriate priority' of the change is undecidable from request, policy and seed, so the benchmark's vacuous priority IS NOT NULL stays. The acting user USER_057 is an active admin, so policy 2 allows every write. No stay requirements: PRB_010 is the only malware or tablet problem, the change and mapping are keyed exactly, the three recipients are fixed by the seed, the task's tools list no incident search so the other tablet incidents (INC_021, INC_039, INC_043) cannot be swept in, and nothing in the request or policy forbids a row.
revised: the mapping requirement's cells no longer repeat change_id, incident_id and problem_id, and the three notification requirements' cells no longer repeat incident_id and email, since each selector already fixes those columns; the sql, counts and dispositions are unchanged.
